items.title: Al Rose Interview, 1975-02-03
items.q: I had to get them to call backstage and Muggsy Spank came out and identified me and we went in.

ctx.x: Oh. What about, did you, did you have any trouble, uh, getting in? Have I, didn't you tell me something about that once? Are you, people didn't recognize you as the producer?

Oh, yeah. I, um, uh, I particularly had written that thing about the time I was in Symphony Hall in Boston running a concert there. And, uh, I had gone out for a cup of coffee or sandwich or something. And on my way back in, uh, the guard wouldn't let me in because he assumed that I was a kid trying to crash it. And when I explained to him who I was, he didn't believe me. And at last I had to get them to call backstage and Muggsy Spank came out and identified me and we went in. How many journeys into jazz…

Well, I can, uh, I put on a few things, uh, myself, and I find it very depressing. When you try to, even though people may be in the right idiom, I still don't think they understand it. I have the right attitude sometimes. They, I don't.
